title: Chinese Carmakers Overtake Japanese Rivals in Europe
paragraphs: Chinese car brands have overtaken their Japanese rivals in Europe, marking a significant shift in one of the world's most important car markets.

According to data from the market research firm Dataforce, Chinese brands accounted for 12.7% of new car registrations in Europe in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 11.9% for Japanese carmakers. It was the first time Chinese brands had outsold Japanese brands over a full quarter. In September alone, Chinese brands achieved a record market share of 14.5%.

The milestone had been approaching for several months. Data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association showed that Chinese brands first overtook Japanese brands on a monthly basis in May. They remained ahead in June, when their share of the European market reached 13%, up from 7.9% a year earlier.
The speed of this growth has surprised much of the industry, including many experienced analysts. Five years ago, Chinese brands accounted for only about 1% of European car sales.

Much of the recent growth has come from hybrid vehicles, including plug-in hybrids. This is partly because of trade rules. In 2024, the European Union introduced additional tariffs on electric vehicles made in China, but these tariffs do not apply to hybrids. As a result, Chinese carmakers have increasingly focused on hybrid models for the European market. They have also been expanding their manufacturing operations within Europe itself.

For Japanese carmakers, the trend is a serious and growing challenge. Japanese brands have long been known for their hybrid technology, and they are currently defending their position in Europe mainly with petrol and hybrid models. Now they face strong competition in this area from Chinese companies.
Nevertheless, European manufacturers such as Volkswagen and Renault continue to hold the top positions in their home market.

Some analysts believe that Chinese growth may slow in the future. Beatrix Keim of the Center Automotive Research recently lowered her forecast for Chinese brands' share of the European market in 2035, from 20% to 15%. Even so, the latest figures show that Chinese brands have quickly become a major force in Europe's car industry.
